name: Economic Research Service homepage: a government data portal landing page
title: Economic Research Service homepage: a government data portal landing page
answer: The Economic Research Service homepage is a government landing page for economic data on food, farming, natural resources, and rural America. Its most useful content for agriculture is a set of links to ERS State Fact Sheets, the Food Price Outlook, and Vegetables and Pulses Data. The page itself does not mention precision agriculture, variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, autonomous equipment, or AI adoption. A reader looking for ERS measurement of US precision agriculture adoption will not find it in this harvested text, only a gateway to other ERS products.

sections.body: The Economic Research Service publishes this page. It is the homepage of the Economic Research Service, a .gov service. The page covers the economics of food, farming, natural resources, and rural America. The harvested text is dated September 26, 2026 and gives no publication date for the page itself. It is a landing page that highlights selected ERS data products and an email notification service, not a report, dataset, or methodology document. It does not mention precision agriculture adoption or any related technology.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page describes several ERS products. The ERS State Fact Sheets provide information on population, income, poverty, food security, education, employment, farm characteristics, farm financial indicators, top commodities, and agricultural exports. Data are available for all States, and for metro and nonmetro breakouts within States, and for Puerto Rico if applicable. Links to county-level data are provided where available. The Food Price Outlook provides food price data and forecasts changes in the Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index for food. Vegetables and Pulses Data is a collection of resources that provide comprehensive statistics on fresh and processed vegetables and dry pulses in the United States, as well as some global data for these sectors. The page also invites readers to subscribe to an email notification service to receive announcements of the latest reports and other news shown on the ERS calendar. It includes a standard government website security notice about .gov addresses. The text does not describe precision agriculture, variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, autonomous equipment, or farm adoption rates for any of these technologies. It is a short gateway page rather than a detailed source.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numeric figures. It states that ERS State Fact Sheets cover all States, metro and nonmetro breakouts within States, and Puerto Rico if applicable, with county-level links where available. It states that the Food Price Outlook forecasts changes in the Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index for food. It states that Vegetables and Pulses Data covers fresh and processed vegetables and dry pulses in the United States and some global data. It gives no precision agriculture adoption figures, no definitions of variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, or autonomous equipment, and no AI adoption claims.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in agriculture would find this source useful only as a pointer to ERS economic data, not as evidence about AI or precision agriculture adoption. The page can lead to State Fact Sheets with farm characteristics and financial indicators, to food price forecasts, and to vegetable and pulse statistics. Those products may provide baseline context for agricultural economics. However, the harvested text does not support the industry page's claim that ERS measures US adoption of precision agriculture, variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, or autonomous equipment. For AI adoption specifically, this source offers no data, definitions, or findings.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Agriculture

sections.body: This is a landing page, not a report or dataset. It does not cover precision agriculture, variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, autonomous equipment, or AI adoption. It gives no publication date, methodology, sample size, or adoption rates. It is a government page, not commercial, but it is partial because it only highlights selected ERS products and an email subscription. The harvested text is dated September 26, 2026, so any linked content may have changed. A reader should treat it as a gateway and check the linked ERS products directly for substantive data.
